method_limits: the population is E437's, imported rather than re-derived: same corpus, same parameter sites, same call-row unit, same temp marker text; a disagreement between this face and namerecall_latest.json is a defect in this file, not a new measurement

write paths are the ones the scan already classified as path writes (open for writing, write_text/write_bytes, the pandas/image save family); a write performed by a callee this function calls is not followed, so C_INSIDE means 'this function spells a path inside the directory', not 'the bytes definitely land there'

a function that writes nothing is not a write site and never enters the population, so the 'composes a name and someone else writes it' case is outside this scan -- it is published as a blind spot and is NOT counted in C_OUTSIDE

join detection covers four spellings (os.path.join, Path(p)/x, p + '/x', f'{p}/x'); a path built by a helper that takes the directory as an argument reads as W_NAMED, which is reported as its own class rather than folded into inside or outside
a callee with several directory parameters is graded over all of them, so a write that composes onto parameter B is counted as inside even when the row supplied A

directory_passed_to_a_file_path_paramete.reading: these call rows hand a directory to a callee whose only write is the parameter path itself (json.dump/save/write_json wrappers); the directory lands on a file slot, so nothing is written inside it and the call would fail if it ever ran against the real path

title: grade every temp-supplying directory-parameter call row by whether the callee's write paths compose a name onto the supplied directory
